---
title: "Shared exponential kernel calculations"
description: "Replay numeric exponential states through a public, baseline-independent API."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(emhawkes)
```

## Purpose and availability

The GitHub development version 1.0.1.9000 exports `exp_kernel_spec()`,
`as_exp_kernel()` and `exp_kernel_replay()`. These experimental functions provide
a shared calculation boundary inside emhawkes. The separate
[frpp package](https://ksublee.github.io/frpp/) uses it for its numeric `state`
likelihood. The dependency is frpp -> emhawkes.

The API supplies kernel states and integrals. The calling model owns its
baseline, initialization policy, residual distribution, likelihood and random
draws. Existing Hawkes event loops and `emhawkes.engine` selection are unchanged.
Publication on GitHub does not update an already installed CRAN version.

## Specification and mapping

Numeric alpha and beta are D by K matrices; eta is optional with the same shape.
Beta must be positive and equal within each row. Rows are event types and
columns are kernels. `type_col_map[[i]]` selects the columns updated by type i;
entries can overlap across event types. Signed components and jumps are retained.
These shape rules alone do not guarantee a valid simulator or stationarity.
Function-valued kernel parameters and impact callbacks are outside this first
interface; conversion rejects them without executing them.

```{r kernel}
h <- new("hspec", mu = c(.3, .4),
  alpha = matrix(c(.04, .03, .02, .05, .01, .02, .03, .01), 2, 4),
  beta = matrix(rep(c(1.2, 1.7), 4), 2),
  type_col_map = list(c(3L, 1L), c(2L, 4L)))
kernel <- as_exp_kernel(h)
```

`as_exp_kernel()` reads kernel slots only. Baselines, mark generators, mark
densities and residual laws are not copied or evaluated. The specification
contains no evolving state, so replaying it twice does not accumulate events.

## Replay contract

Supply observed intervals, types, optional marks and explicit initial components.
The first row is the initial state: its interval is zero and it causes no event
update. Subsequent zero intervals update events in input order. Replay adds no
terminal observation interval and consumes no random numbers.

```{r replay}
dt <- c(0, .2, .4, 0, .3)
type <- c(0, 1, 2, 1, 2)
initial <- matrix(.05, 2, 4)
x <- exp_kernel_replay(kernel, dt, type, lambda_component0 = initial)
x$kernel_integral
x$kernel_before
x$final_component
```

For M input rows, the ordinary output is:

| Output | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kernel_integral` | M by D | Kernel-only integral over each interval; initial row is zero |
| `kernel_before` | M by D | Pre-event component sums; initial row is the initial row sums |
| `final_component` | D by K | State after the final event, or unchanged initial state for M = 1 |

A scalar initial value expands over all components. A matrix must match D by K;
a matching vector follows R's column-major matrix order. Automatic mean/zero
policies and count paths belong to the calling model.

With `history = TRUE`, `component_before` and `component_after` are additionally
returned as M by (D times K). Within each row, components are flattened row by
row. Histories are allocated only when requested. Ordinary output still stores
M by D interval integrals and sums; it is not constant-memory streaming.

```{r history}
full <- exp_kernel_replay(kernel, dt, type, lambda_component0 = initial,
  history = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(x, full[names(x)]))
```

## Using the result in another model

For a numeric baseline mu, the caller forms pre-event drivers and integrated
drivers as follows:

```{r baseline}
mu <- as.vector(h@mu)
driver_before <- sweep(x$kernel_before, 2, mu, "+")
integrated_driver <- x$kernel_integral + outer(dt, mu)
driver_before
integrated_driver
```

FRPP combines these with residual density and survival terms. A non-exponential
residual law changes the conditional hazard: the kernel driver by itself is
not automatically the FRPP conditional intensity. Hawkes-specific stationary
means, gradients and Hessian adjustments are not supplied by this API.

Use the exported functions rather than `emhawkes:::`. The implementation is an
R reference path, independent of the likelihood engine option. Internal
advance/update helpers and C++ implementation details are not part of this
public contract. Event-wise calculations below support independent FRPP event
generation; callback kernels remain outside this numeric interface.


## Event-wise calculations

`exp_kernel_wait()` inverts supplied integrated-driver targets using a numeric
baseline and current kernel components. It draws no residuals and selects no
event. `exp_kernel_step()` advances the components and optionally applies one
mapped event; it also returns component integrals unless `integrate = FALSE`.
Neither function replays a growing path prefix.

```{r event-wise}
component <- initial
candidates <- exp_kernel_wait(kernel, component, mu, residual = c(.7, .9))
event <- which.min(candidates)
next_state <- exp_kernel_step(kernel, component, min(candidates), type = event)
next_state$before
next_state$after
next_state$integral
```

A zero interval still updates the selected event. `type = NULL` performs only
decay and integration. Signed components are retained. Waiting-time inversion
requires admissible decreasing row sums; a finite total driver integral can
produce an infinite waiting time when its baseline is zero.

For repeated calculations with fixed parameters, prepare a reusable plan:

```{r prepared-plan}
plan <- exp_kernel_plan(kernel, mu)
stopifnot(identical(candidates, plan$wait(component, c(.7, .9))))
stopifnot(identical(next_state, plan$step(component, min(candidates), event)))
```

The plan captures a validated kernel and baseline once. Its `wait()` and `step()`
functions still check the changing components and arguments. Components remain
explicit inputs: the plan stores no event state, history or RNG. It is reusable
across independent paths; create a new plan when parameters change. Editing the
original specification does not change an existing plan. The plan's function
bindings are locked. Older event-wise functions remain available with their
existing checked input contracts.

FRPP owns its residual-generation order, earliest-event selection, count paths,
output histories and RNG handling. The event-wise API receives explicit targets
and contains no model-specific residual law. Legacy Hawkes and FRPP event loops
are unchanged. This is an R reference interface, not a speed improvement claim.

## Parameter registration and restoration

`parameter_plan()` supplies model-independent parameter coordinates. Supply a
named component list and mark explicit parameter-vector components with `named`.
Equal values within a numeric matrix share a parameter under `reduced = TRUE`;
explicit named vectors retain distinct parameters even when their values match.
Names shared across components identify one coordinate. Conflicting starts warn
and use the first value, following the existing hfit rule.

```{r parameter-registration}
parameters <- parameter_plan(list(mu = h@mu, alpha = h@alpha, beta = h@beta,
  residual = c(shape = 2, rate = 2)), named = "residual")
parameters$start
values <- parameters$restore(parameters$start)
stopifnot(identical(values$alpha, h@alpha),
  identical(values$residual, c(shape = 2, rate = 2)))
```

The locked plan stores definitions and coordinates, not fitted model state.
Restoration returns components for the caller to assemble. It accepts the full
vector in starting order, or exactly its names in any order. Nonfinite proposals
are preserved for the objective to reject. Fixed/free selection, bounds and
constraints use these coordinates and remain optimizer responsibilities.

Function components retain their original environments and binding behavior.
Their `param` defaults are evaluated during registration; function bodies are
not called. User default expressions can have side effects. Existing hfit maps
and saved-fit metadata retain their original representation.
